solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Copper checks over practice

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: over signals turning the word for checks the other way round

parts.note: MOTs are the annual roadworthiness checks on British vehicles

explanation.surface: A policeman inspects some long-standing practice or procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer but gives the symbol CU; 'over' turns MOTS (the British annual vehicle test) into STOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a habitual practice or tradition, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Cold old Latvian perhaps in his element

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a Latvian is one example of a Balt, a native of the Baltic states

explanation.surface: An elderly man from Latvia, feeling the chill yet perfectly at home and comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In his element' reads as an idiom for being comfortable, but the last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a metallic chemical element, atomic number 27.

clue.text: Alpine event 6 covering half of June

indicators.note: covering means the stingy word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: the answer to 6 down means behave stingily, which is to skimp

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of June

explanation.surface: A winter event in the mountains scheduled to run into early June.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 6 (PENNY-PINCH) must first be swapped for a synonym before 'covering' can act on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski jumping is a classic competition held in Alpine resorts and at the Winter Olympics.

clue.text: Old poet's current disease beginning to disappear

indicators.note: the first letter of the disease's name is made to vanish

parts.note: Covid is the disease of the present day

explanation.surface: A modern illness afflicting a classical writer, now starting to fade.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet of the Augustan age, author of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Careless errors by head office department

parts.note: slips are small mistakes

explanation.surface: Mistakes made by a company's headquarters staff are put down to sloppiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod work is done hastily and without care, so it describes careless behaviour.

clue.text: Reformulated all-in-one lotion

indicators.note: reformulated means made up again in a new recipe, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cosmetics firm has relaunched its multi-purpose skin cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformulated' rearranges the letters of ALL-IN-ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanoline, the fat from sheep's wool, is a base for skin ointments and creams.

clue.text: Behave like Scrooge with 2p in church

parts.note: two p's: one written out as penny and one as the letter itself

explanation.surface: A miser's gesture: dropping a mere two pence in the church collection.
explanation.walkthrough: '2p' gives both of its p's: one as the word PENNY, the other as the letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrooge, Dickens's miser, is a byword for stinginess, which is what being a penny-pincher means.

clue.text: She's writer, looking run down

definitions.meaning: the author of the adventure novel She is H. Rider ...
means gaunt and exhausted in appearance

explanation.surface: A woman who writes is looking worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is not a pronoun but the title of an 1887 novel, so 'She's writer' is its author.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggard means drawn and tired-looking; Rider Haggard wrote She and King Solomon's Mines.

clue.text: Battle at the Belfry?

definitions.meaning: a fierce, closely fought contest or row
the sound heard from bells in a bell tower

explanation.walkthrough: The Belfry is also a famous English golf course that has hosted the Ryder Cup, adding to the sporting-battle feel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ding-dong is a slang term for a heated fight, and it imitates the chime of bells.

clue.text: Old king left rubbish

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch abandoned his trash.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was the Anglo-Saxon ruler of Mercia who built Offa's Dyke along the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal, besides meaning animal entrails, is used for refuse or worthless scraps.

clue.text: Trouble during strike for serving officer

indicators.note: during places the trouble word within the strike word

parts.note: a biff is a blow or punch
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Unrest during an industrial walkout involves an officer on active duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but it means a blow, BIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff is a court official who serves writs and summonses, hence an officer who does the serving.

clue.text: Figure 12 captivates Harry

indicators.note: captivates means holds captive, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: twelve o'clock in the day is noon
to harry is to pester or nag

explanation.surface: A numerical value charms a man called Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a cross-reference to 12 across but simply stands for midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a nine-sided polygon, a geometrical figure.

clue.text: Flashy student with Open University departs

parts.note: L for learner is a student driver's plate
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A showy learner leaves along with the Open University.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is a British distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud is used of clothes or colours that are garish and showy.

clue.text: Lanky Jane's not finished with former French diplomat

parts.note: lanky means tall and thin

indicators.note: not finished removes the last letter of the surname

parts.note: Jane Eyre is Charlotte Bronte's heroine
and is a synonym for with

explanation.surface: A tall, thin woman named Jane is still at work alongside an old French envoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jane' needs her famous surname, EYRE, which 'not finished' cuts to EYR.
explanation.definitionFit: Talleyrand was the wily French foreign minister under Napoleon and at the Congress of Vienna.

clue.text: Gullible type nicks English queen's material

indicators.note: nicks here means cuts into, so the other letters enter the gullible word

parts.note: a sucker is someone easily fooled
ER (Elizabeth Regina) with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A dupe pinches a fabric belonging to an English queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicks' suggests stealing but means cutting into: EERS goes after the S of SUCKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a puckered cotton fabric, so it is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Drug rush

explanation.definitionFit: Speed is street slang for amphetamines, and to speed is to rush along.

clue.text: A foreign VP once hosted Democrat spontaneously

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: hosted means took in, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Joe Biden was US vice-president under Obama

explanation.surface: A former vice-president from abroad entertained a party colleague on impulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A foreign' means the word for 'a' in a foreign language, here French.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbidden means without being asked, of one's own accord, as spontaneous action is.

clue.text: Weirdo takes one drug after another

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: An oddball works through a series of narcotics one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person, a synonym for an odd character.

clue.text: Leaves box made of pine wrapped in paper

indicators.note: wrapped in puts the yearning word inside the paper word

parts.note: an exam paper is a test
to pine is to ache or yearn

explanation.surface: A crate for leaves, built of pine timber and packed in paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the wood the box is made of but is the verb, ACHE; 'leaves' are tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is the wooden crate in which loose tea leaves were shipped.

clue.text: First of ripostes with sword involving skill and wit

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word ripostes
involving means taking in, so the skill word goes inside the sword word

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword
art means skill

explanation.surface: A fencer's ripostes show swordplay, skill and sharp wit.
explanation.walkthrough: A riposte is both a fencing counter-thrust and a quick verbal reply, so the surface fits either reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, witty conversational exchange, so the word stands for verbal wit.

clue.text: Superior music company cuts drink under pressure

indicators.note: in a down answer, under puts the drink below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the record company goes inside the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit
EMI is a well-known record company

explanation.surface: A top record label cuts spirits under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Premium as an adjective means of the highest quality, superior grade.

clue.text: Young reporter blocking South Africa tanks

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, so the reporter sits inside the country's letters

parts.note: a cub reporter is a novice journalist

explanation.surface: A junior journalist obstructs South African armoured vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanks' suggests armour but means diving air tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuba gear is self-contained breathing apparatus, essentially air tanks for divers.

clue.text: Jerk lifts this, omitting source of 8

parts.note: bar means except or omitting
the answer to 8 down is the chime of a bell, so a bell is its source

explanation.surface: A weightlifter's jerk raises this, leaving out where the chime comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' is the weightlifting lift (clean and jerk), not an insult; 'omitting' is the word BAR, not a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbell is the long weighted bar raised in the clean and jerk.

clue.text: Note goes round old police: "Ceasefire!"

indicators.note: goes round means encircles, so the note wraps the police letters

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's former force

explanation.surface: A message is passed among former police officers calling a halt to shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreement to stop fighting, which a ceasefire declares.

clue.text: Outbid doctor holding unlimited cash

indicators.note: holding means the doctor's letters surround the rest

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner

indicators.note: unlimited strips off both outer letters of the slang money word

parts.note: mazuma is slang for money

explanation.surface: A doctor carrying unlimited money puts in a higher offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The cash word is uncommon slang. Gazumping is a British property-market practice: a seller accepts a higher offer after agreeing a price.
explanation.definitionFit: To gazump is to outbid a buyer after a sale has been agreed, especially for a house.

clue.text: Guarantee European picked up Jack for one

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a Czech is a European from the Czech Republic
a jack is one example of a playing card

explanation.surface: A European is vouched for after collecting a man called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is a playing card, not a name. A cheque card, once common in Britain, guaranteed a shop that a cheque would be honoured.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque guarantee card assured payees that the bank would honour the cheque up to a limit.

clue.text: Tommy and his mates caught a big fish

parts.note: a Tommy is a British private soldier, and with his comrades forms the other ranks, OR
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A soldier and his friends landed a large fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is a slang name for a British private soldier; privates are among the other ranks (OR).
explanation.definitionFit: An orca, the killer whale, is a huge sea creature; loosely calling it a fish is the clue's liberty.

clue.text: Ring service about port

indicators.note: about signals turning the service's abbreviation around

parts.note: the RAF is one of the armed services
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Phone the armed services about a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call but is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is a coastal city and harbour in the Algarve, southern Portugal.

clue.text: Needle Republican in hot water

indicators.note: in puts the Republican's letter inside the trouble word

parts.note: being in a pickle means being in trouble, or hot water

explanation.surface: Taunt a Republican politician who is in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To prickle is to sting or irritate, which is to needle someone.

clue.text: Switzerland demolished a top- class castle

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)
demolished in the sense of ate up, devoured
U stands for upper class

explanation.surface: A first-rate Swiss fortress has been knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demolished' suggests destruction but means ATE, as in polishing off a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or grand country house.

clue.text: Crime writer Josephine pens Award for Audacity

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the novelist's surname surrounds the award

parts.note: Josephine Tey wrote The Daughter of Time
a merit is an award or commendation

explanation.surface: A detective novelist wins a prize for daring.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is reckless boldness, a synonym for audacity or nerve.

clue.text: Serving party by returning vote

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the vote word is read backwards

parts.note: a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: A party in power is serving after a re-run ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a helping or portion of food, as in a serving of mash.
